population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. 18.1% of US adults currently on an incretin drug (all reasons), 27% ever. Arithmetic: ever 27.0 − current 18.1 = 8.9 pts used and off now; ~65% of ever-users have stopped at least once (17.5 pts), of whom 8.9 are off and 8.6 are back on (≈47% of current users are restarters); ~1.4 of the 8.9 off restarted once and stopped again, so 10.0/27.0 ≈ 37% of ever-users have cycled; 10.0/17.5 ≈ 57% cumulative restart over a 2–3-year window, consistent with the parent's 36–47% within one year; never-stopped users = 9.5 pts, about a third of ever-users, consistent with ~34–36% one-year persistence. Income: middle third has nearly caught the top because $149–349 cash orals are within reach of salaried households who lost employer coverage; the bottom third trails because employer retreat hit hourly workers first and only ~18 state Medicaid programs plus DC cover obesity. Age: 65+ nearly doubled (9%→17%) on the extended Medicare Bridge; 50–64 still peaks (28%). Off-drug population is large and visible: ~8.9% of adults have used and stopped, mostly for cost (employer plan change) or GI intolerance. Self-reported adult obesity ~34.5% (from 36.4%), with the decline concentrated in the top two income thirds. Pediatric: ~0.8% of under-18s on drug, almost all 12–17 on-label; under-12 use fell after six states barred it outside trials and specialist prescribing elsewhere became more defensive; affluent skew persists.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended by CMS through Dec 2028 at unchanged ~$245/month to Medicare, ~$50 copay, BMI/comorbidity criteria; permanent status unresolved. Medicaid: ~18 states plus DC cover obesity at the same negotiated rate; the rest cover diabetes and cardiovascular codes only. TRICARE and most state employee plans cover diabetes and established-CVD use only.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 50+ generic brands, ~$6–40/month after a continued price war. Canada: multiple generic semaglutide products, ~CAD 70–110/month. China: domestic generic semaglutide launched 2026–27 and exported to Southeast Asia and the Gulf. Brazil and Mexico generics on market. Generic semaglutide available in roughly 160 countries. US: no FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide; exclusivity to ~2031–32.
access.note: Two tiers have hardened. Tier 1 (covered): T2D and established-CVD codes, Medicare Bridge, some Medicaid; copays ~$25–50. Tier 2 (cash): oral starting doses $149 (Wegovy pill, Foundayo), oral maintenance $299–349, injectable pens on TrumpRx/manufacturer channels $299–349 (the promised $245 never reached the cash channel), retatrutide $799 via LillyDirect under allocation; list prices unchanged (Wegovy $1,349, retatrutide $1,299). Tier 3 (gray): with 503B compounding closed (FDA final exclusion, Oct 2027) and Florida's Section 804 import of Canadian generics enjoined on patent grounds, demand moved to personal-importation mail order of Canadian and Indian generic pens (~$60–100/month) and 'research peptide' sellers; FDA seizure notices rising but volume not quantified. Employer coverage for weight management fell to 43% (BGH, 2028 plan year); nearly all employers that dropped it retain coverage under diabetes and CVD codes, so coding at diagnosis now decides who pays. Orals are ~40% of new starts; weekly injectables remain the majority of continuing users.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026 for chronic weight management; modest uptake after REDEFINE-4)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Apr 2028 for chronic weight management; launched under supply allocation)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet' / calm-and-focus low-dose use marketed by telehealth programs (e.g. Stillwell's Quiet) to people without obesity, framed as freedom from craving; FDA bars drug-name claims, so programs sell the service rather than the molecule
alcohol reduction — phase 3 AUD trials of semaglutide underway; no approval; clinicians prescribe off-label to patients with obesity plus heavy drinking
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use by people without obesity, via telehealth (now restricted to BMI ≥27 for telehealth initiation in Texas and Florida)
reward/craving reduction for nicotine and gambling — observational and anecdotal
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, now barred outside trials in six states
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide: BLA filed Feb 2027 (per the parent's ~Q1 2027 plan), approved Apr 2028 after a 14-month review, >12 months after filing as required. Label: 28.7% mean loss at 80 weeks at top dose (up to ~30% in BMI ≥35), dysesthesia and ~11% adverse-event discontinuation carried from phase 3, lean-mass language in clinical-studies section. Launched under allocation; Lilly prioritises patients already on tirzepatide and covered BMI ≥35 patients, and cites capacity until new fill-finish plants come online 2029. This is the step's ~30% 'surgical-grade' pen. No new indication beyond weight management. CagriSema approved Dec 2026 within its review window. Amycretin remains in phase 3; no filing, cannot be on market. Survodutide phase 3 read out; no US filing this step. MariTide monthly injectable in phase 3, not on market. Semaglutide AUD phase 3 enrolling; no sNDA. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) in phase 2/3. Global incretin market ~$110B (2028); US net price per script flat, volume growing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect; concentrated at initiation and dose escalation; still the leading clinical cause of discontinuation, though cost has overtaken it as the leading overall cause among working-age stoppers. Retatrutide's GI profile is similar to tirzepatide's at matched escalation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis' (Jan 2025) unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; clinicians watching retatrutide users given larger, faster loss.
Long-term RCTs still have not confirmed a causal link; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; product-liability litigation ongoing, no resolution.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass; concern sharpened by the doubling of use among Medicare beneficiaries and by retatrutide's larger absolute losses; bone and musculoskeletal signal from 2026 AAOS abstract not yet confirmed or refuted.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None beyond label text; industry response is adjunct trials; geriatric societies issue resistance-training and protein guidance.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; no new data changed the picture.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide stands; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association (EMA, MHRA, 2025 systematic review).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA's January 2026 removal of the warning from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels stands.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still unquantified; no trial designed to detect it has reported. Now also the selling point of 'quiet' telehealth programs, whose marketing cites unpublished intake surveys. Clinicians describe it as dose-related and reversible on reduction; no new data moved its status.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None as a safety matter. FDA's Oct 2027 telehealth advertising enforcement policy treats calm/focus claims tied to a named drug as off-label promotion, which governs the marketing, not the effect.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial data (~two-thirds regained within a year) and gentler real-world claims data still conflict; the large cost-driven off-drug population makes regain a common lived experience.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; underpins chronic-therapy framing and Medicare persistence requirements.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reduced-intake deficiencies flagged in reviews; relevant to retatrutide's deeper appetite suppression; no confirmatory trial.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exists for semaglutide; nothing on cycling, which over a third of ever-users have done, or on adolescents across development.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on Foundayo, CagriSema and retatrutide; cited by six states as grounds for under-12 limits.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Compounded supply largely gone after 503B exclusion; risk has moved to imported generic and counterfeit pens and 'research peptides' bought by mail, where dose and provenance are unverifiable. Adverse-event reporting continues at a lower but steady rate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised Oct 2027; FDA import alerts and seizure notices; personal-importation discretion not withdrawn.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households ~30% of US households. Salty snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks lose a further ~2–3% volume a year; big CPG portfolios lean on protein, fibre, minis and 'companion' lines and hold revenue through price and mix. Stalled drug prices and employer retreat slow the curve below 2026 forecasts, so JPMorgan-style 2030 loss estimates are revised toward the low end. A small premium counter-current in a few metros (Brooklyn, Austin, LA) sells full-fat, full-portion products on 'come hungry' branding.

alcohol.state: US spirits and wine volumes keep falling (spirits ~−4% in 2027); Diageo and Brown-Forman cut US guidance again, citing heavy drinkers shifting down; non-alcoholic and low-ABV grow but do not offset; on-drug drinkers buy fewer, pricier 'occasion' drinks. Off-label AUD prescribing removes some of the heaviest buyers.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat; chains standardise half-portion and 'lighter plate' menus and protein add-ons; check averages held up by premium items. In the Austin and Brooklyn independent trade, 'long table' family-style dinners with no half portions market hearty eating to the unmedicated-signalling crowd, a niche that sells out and sets press narratives.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep closing stores and shrinking size runs; DXL and Torrid both cite on-drug customers. Mainstream retailers carry fewer extended sizes. A small growth segment in LA-based labels cuts 'athletic fit' for muscle rather than slimness.

fitness.state: Strength floors expand at budget chains; premium clubs sell 'taper' and muscle-retention programs to people coming off or dosing down; DEXA-scan studios spread in LA and Miami; Medicare Advantage plans pay for resistance-training classes for members on GLP-1s.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management down to 43% (BGH, 2028); coverage concentrated on T2D and established-CVD codes, so primary-care coding is contested and audited; PBMs run carve-out cash programs; Medicare Bridge extended at $245; Medicaid split by state. Pharmacy trend moderates as employers shift cost to employees.

pharma.state: Lilly dominant (tirzepatide, Foundayo, retatrutide); Novo restructured, leaning on oral Wegovy and CagriSema. US net prices flat by design and by allocation; volume up; ex-US revenue squeezed by generics. Global incretin market ~$110B in 2028.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among the middle-aged insured and the cash-paying salaried middle, a newly lean body reads as 'on it' and is unremarkable. In the Los Angeles casting and talent-management trade and in Brooklyn and Austin restaurant-and-music circles, slimness has lost its signal; visible muscle and eating heartily in public read as rare, and as 'unmedicated'.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness has moved down from the top third into the middle, carried by $149–349 cash orals, which is why it lost status at the top. It has not reached the bottom: hourly workers lost employer coverage first and Medicaid is split, so obesity is increasingly concentrated in the lowest-income third and among the uninsured working-age. The new ideal (muscle, appetite, 'unmedicated vitality') costs time, trainers and food, and stays scarce.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In GLP-1 households, small portions, protein-first plates and eating for duty rather than desire. In the Austin and Brooklyn trades that set taste, the 'long table' (seconds unasked, plates photographed empty) works as a status ritual. Family dinners where half the table is on drug and half is not are a common sitcom premise.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: In Brooklyn and Austin dating scenes, 'are you on it' is a routine early question and 'unmedicated' appears as a profile line; couples therapists in Austin describe 'mismatched quiet' when one partner is on a low 'quiet' dose. Still anecdotal; not quantified.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the circles where the inversion runs, appetite has turned from a symptom into a credential: 'hungry' is a compliment, eating openly a display. In the clinic and the payer's office it is still a treatable signal. Both readings hold at once, sorted by class.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Still unmeasured by any trial; ledger status 'emerging'. Telehealth 'quiet' programs cite their own unpublished intake surveys (Stillwell claims ~70% of subscribers report 'less noise'). Clinicians describe the effect as dose-related and reversible on dose reduction. Roughly 350,000 people are subscribed to programs that sell it as the point.
interior_life.framing: Two framings coexist. On the label and in the clinic it is a side effect or nothing. In the wellness market it is 'quiet': calm, focus, freedom from craving, sold as a service. FDA rules forced the drug names out of the copy; the product stayed.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Low-dose 'quiet' is popular among commodity traders in Chicago and enterprise-sales staff in Austin, who describe evenness, fewer impulse decisions and no 3 p.m. snack spiral. Some managers like the steadiness; others report reps who stop chasing quota. No employer program endorses it, and several firms' benefits teams have ruled lifestyle-spending accounts ineligible for it.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: In LA comedy rooms and the Nashville songwriting trade, 'unmedicated' is a credential and an open-mic bit; some performers taper before tours and say so publicly. Brooklyn venues report lower bar spend per head. Intensity products (extreme sour, superhot sauces, high-stimulation rhythm games) sell to on-drug buyers looking for a felt reward.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reported reduced desire in some users, and now a deliberate trade-off for 'quiet' subscribers, some of whom say they want less longing. Couples therapists in Austin and Denver describe partners on different doses negotiating dose timing around anniversaries and holidays.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Restriction politics run on two vocabularies: MAHA-aligned state legislators use 'unmedicated vitality' and 'children's natural development' to pass under-12 limits, while obesity-medicine groups call the limits, the BMI caps and the employer retreat class policy. The US–Canada price gap and the Florida import injunction are 2028 primary-season talking points. No measurable effect of blunting itself on turnout or engagement.

state.regulatory_posture: Fast at the centre, restrictive at the edges. FDA approves retatrutide and CagriSema on schedule but finalises the 503B compounding exclusion and, in Oct 2027, an enforcement policy treating telehealth ads tied to a dispensing arrangement as drug promotion, which bans calm/focus/lifestyle claims and influencer endorsements that name a GLP-1. States add age limits and prescribing rules.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge extended through Dec 2028 at unchanged $245/$50; ~18 state Medicaid programs plus DC cover obesity; TrumpRx cash channel continues at $299–349 for injectables, $149 for oral starting doses.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage conditioned on diagnosis codes (T2D, established CVD), BMI thresholds and prior authorisation; payers audit coding. Six states (including Tennessee, Utah, Louisiana and Oklahoma) bar prescribing under 12 outside clinical trials and require specialist initiation for 12–17. Texas and Florida require an in-person visit before telehealth GLP-1 initiation and cap telehealth initiation at BMI ≥27. No adherence surveillance beyond Medicare persistence checks.
state.workforce_or_military: No mandate or employer program. DoD accession guidance requires documented weight stability for applicants who used GLP-1s to meet body-composition standards; recruiters in the South report applicants affected. TRICARE covers diabetes and cardiac use only.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US brand exclusivity holds to ~2031–32 while India, China, Canada, Brazil and Mexico sell generics; a federal court enjoined Florida's Section 804 import of Canadian generic semaglutide on patent grounds (2027); Chinese generic exports grow in Asia and the Gulf; US mail-order personal importation becomes the pressure valve the government tolerates and the manufacturers litigate around. Retatrutide capacity is a Lilly manufacturing constraint, not a geopolitical one.

events.event: Miami telehealth firm Stillwell launches 'Quiet', a $199/month clinician-led low-dose oral semaglutide program sold for 'calm, focus and freedom from craving' to adults without obesity; passes 200,000 subscribers within a year

Business Group on Health: share of large employers covering GLP-1s for weight management in 2028 falls to 43% from 60%; nearly all keep coverage under type 2 diabetes and established-cardiovascular-disease codes

FDA finalises exclusion of semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from 503B compounding and issues a telehealth advertising enforcement policy barring lifestyle claims and influencer endorsements of named GLP-1s; by January six states have barred under-12 prescribing outside trials and Texas and Florida require in-person initiation with a BMI ≥27 floor

CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through December 2028 at an unchanged $245/month and $50 copay; Lilly and Novo hold cash pens at $299–349, citing Medicare volume and capacity, after a federal court in June enjoined Florida's import of Canadian generic semaglutide on patent grounds

FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide for chronic weight management, 14 months after filing, with a label showing 28.7% mean loss at 80 weeks; Lilly launches under supply allocation at $1,299 list and $799 cash

A Los Angeles casting breakdown for a network drama asking for 'unmedicated, natural build, visible strength' circulates widely; LA talent managers say clients are tapering doses and disclosing it to stay castable

open_tensions: The two-tier system has hardened. Diagnosis codes and age now decide who gets a $50 copay and who pays $349 or buys a pen from Windsor by mail. Obesity is concentrating in the bottom income third, and the Medicare Bridge expires again in December 2028 with nothing permanent behind it.

Blunting is being sold as 'quiet' to hundreds of thousands of people while the ledger still lists it as unmeasured. FDA policy governs the ads, not the effect, and no trial is designed to find out what years of chosen flatness do.

Retatrutide gives surgical-scale loss under allocation, to covered and affluent patients first, just as use among over-65s has doubled. The lean-mass concern is about to be tested at scale in the people least able to spare muscle.

The aesthetic inversion devalues thinness at the top just as it reaches the middle. Meanwhile state age limits and 'unmedicated vitality' rhetoric bear hardest on the adolescents and families who were never inside the first tier.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral GLP-1 starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still priced at $149 a month on the cash channel.
Medicare still pays ~$245 a month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the GLP-1 Bridge, with BMI/comorbidity criteria.
FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels stands; the effect remains classed as debunked.

prose.headline: Thin Got Common: The 30% Pen Arrives, Employers Walk Away, and the People Who Set Taste Start Eating Again
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2028 about eighteen in every hundred American adults take an incretin drug. Nobody is asking whether they work anymore. The questions are who pays, and what being on one says about you.

The first answer has settled into tiers. If your chart says type 2 diabetes or established heart disease, your plan almost certainly covers semaglutide or tirzepatide for a copay. If you are on Medicare, the Bridge pilot that was due to end in December 2027 has been extended another year at the same $245 a month to the government and $50 to you, and use among the over-65s has nearly doubled. If you are working-age and your only diagnosis is obesity, you are more and more on your own. Fewer than half of large employers still cover weight management. They didn't drop it all at once; it went one plan year at a time, and the employers that dropped it kept paying for the diabetes and cardiac codes. A primary-care visit now carries the question of how the chart will be coded.

On your own means cash, and cash has stopped getting cheaper. Oral starting doses still cost $149, but maintenance doses run $299 to $349, and the government's cash channel for pens never reached the promised $245. The manufacturers point to Medicare volume and to capacity. A federal court blocked Florida's plan to import Canadian generic semaglutide on patent grounds. The gap is visible from the border: generic pens cost well under $100 in Canada and a fraction of that in India. With compounding closed, a significant share of the cash tier now buys by mail from Windsor or Hyderabad, in packaging nobody checks.

The new drug is retatrutide, Lilly's triple agonist, approved in April after a fourteen-month review. At the top dose it delivers close to thirty percent weight loss, roughly what a surgeon used to. It launched under allocation at $799 a month cash, so for now it reaches the well-covered and the well-off first, and the first big test of its muscle loss will be in older patients.

Thinness has moved down the income ladder into the salaried middle, and it lost its value at the top in the process. In the Los Angeles casting trade, and in the Brooklyn and Austin restaurant and music circles that set taste, a newly lean fifty-year-old reads as a prescription. What reads as rare is what the drugs wear away or quiet down: visible muscle and visible appetite. Casting breakdowns ask for 'unmedicated'. Independent restaurants run long-table dinners with no half portions and a line on the menu that says come hungry. Strength gyms sell programs for tapering off. None of this has reached the bottom income third, where hourly workers lost coverage first, and where obesity is increasingly concentrated.

The reward-dampening that users complained about in 2026 is now for sale. Telehealth programs such as Stillwell's Quiet sell it at low doses to people with no weight to lose, as calm, focus and freedom from craving. Traders in Chicago and sales staff in Austin talk about evenness. The FDA's 2027 advertising policy removed the drug names from the ads; the customers stayed. On the safety ledger the effect is still listed as emerging, because no trial has measured it, and no new signal has arrived to force one.

The state is fast at the centre and restrictive at the edges. Approvals arrive on schedule. Compounding is gone. Six states bar prescribing to children under twelve outside trials, and Texas and Florida require an in-person visit and a BMI floor before telehealth can start anyone. Snack volumes shrink, spirits contract, plus-size stores close, and strength floors expand. From the outside it looks like a country that has mostly gotten healthier, which by most measures it has. About nine adults in a hundred have taken a drug and stopped, and most of the ones who stop eventually come back.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Reyes wakes at 5:40, takes the pill with a full glass of water and waits thirty minutes for coffee, the way the leaflet says. Foundayo, maintenance dose, $349, on the same card that pays the electric. Until January it was a $25 copay. Then the warehouse where Hector drives a forklift switched plans, and the new one covers it for diabetes, which she doesn't have, by a margin she watches like the weather.

The Thursday special at the restaurant on East Cesar Chavez is the Long Table: six courses served family-style, no half portions, and printed at the bottom of the menu, come hungry. Servers bring seconds without being asked. Marisol makes the mole. She tastes it off the back of a spoon, notes the salt and the burnt-chile edge, and feels nothing pull at her. Chef says she has the cleanest palate on the line. She thinks it may be because nothing is in the way.

A table of eight, all forearms and loud, sends compliments back and asks for more tortillas. One woman photographs her plate before and after. After, it's empty.

On her break her sister texts a link: Canadian pens, $70, ships from Windsor, no prescription questions. Marisol saves it and doesn't answer.

She gets home at eleven. Hector is asleep on the couch with the TV on, playing an ad for something called Quiet: a woman in linen by a window, and the words less noise. Marisol turns it off. In the kitchen she eats four crackers standing up, because she should, and checks the calendar on the fridge. Refill Tuesday.

least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ever-use rises from 15% to 27% in two years, and the candidate has 8.9% off now and 37% cycled. This is a very aggressive build on the 7.1pp adoption delta. Adding 7.1pp of current use would more plausibly raise ever-use by roughly 10–12pp, not 12.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage for weight management fell to 43% (BGH, 2028 plan year)
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: a drop from 60% to 43% in two years is steep, though the driver stipulates employer retreat. The related claim that nearly all dropping employers keep diabetes and CVD coverage is convenient, and the candidate also reports a sharp 'cash price stalled' but the '$245 never reached the cash channel' contradicts the parent's stated trend to $245.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly 350,000 people are subscribed to programs that sell it as the point.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: 200,000 subscribers within a year of a March 2027 launch, 350,000 by 2028, sold off-label to non-obese adults at $199 under FDA ad enforcement. The growth is asserted, and the 'passes 200,000 subscribers' event and the 70% 'less noise' claim rest on unpublished surveys.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder two-tier society: coding at diagnosis decides who pays, obesity concentrates in the bottom third, there is a gray-market importation of unverifiable pens, and 350k people are sold chosen flatness with no trial measuring it. Offsetting this, adult obesity falls and the large majority is better off, so it stays near the middle of the scale. Inequality and epistemic scores carry most of the weight (the blunting effect is unmeasured and FDA governs only the ads).
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: adoption of 18.1% matches 11 + 7.1, price stalled with $299–349 cash, employer retreat to 43%, triple agonist at 28.7%, aesthetic inversion, restriction, and marketed-feature personality. Gaps are thin: 'safety_signal: none' is honoured, but the Medicare Bridge extension and the 65+ doubling are not driven by any listed driver. mechanism: most changes have chains (503B closure to importation, coding to coverage), and the ever-used arithmetic is shown and reconciles. Weaker are the culture inversion, sorted to niche LA/Brooklyn/Austin circles yet asserted to reshape casting, and the Quiet subscriber growth. magnitude: ever-use at 27% and cycled-off numbers are aggressive, the 65+ jump from 9% to 17% is large for a $50-copay pilot with ~10% newly eligible, and the 43% employer figure falls fast. Retatrutide filing and approval timing is plausible given the 2027 BLA plan.
rationale.generativity: Marisol, Hector, the Long Table at East Cesar Chavez, the Windsor pen link and the Quiet ad give concrete scenes with strong texture and implied conflict about cost and coding. The world fields add casting, comedy, couples-therapy and dosing-negotiation vignettes that could each become a film. The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains, though the ending is slightly neat.

least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: ever-use rises from 15% (Gallup, 2026) to 27% in two years, +12 pp against a current-use rise of only +7.1 pp. Reconciling that needs roughly 9 points of stopped users plus heavy cycling, which is at the aggressive edge for 24 months.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Age: 65+ nearly doubled (9%→17%) on the extended Medicare Bridge
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: only ~10% of Medicare enrollees were newly eligible under the BMI/comorbidity criteria, and the Bridge has a $50 copay and prior authorisation. Reaching 17% use among over-65s within ~18 months of launch assumes near-immediate uptake and is aggressive.

magnitude: the parent figure was ~0.6% of children with obesity. 0.8% of all under-18s implies roughly 2–3% of adolescents, or about a tenth of those with obesity, on drug. That is hard to square with the claimed fall in under-12 use, six state bans and 'more defensive' specialist prescribing.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder, with new losers. A two-tier access system is set by diagnosis coding. A large off-drug cycling population (~9% of adults) is cost-driven. Obesity concentrates in the bottom income third, with the Bridge expiring and nothing permanent behind it. Gray-market importation of unverifiable pens is a further public-health loss. 'Quiet' is sold to ~350k people with no trial measuring blunting, which worsens the epistemic picture. Offsets are real: obesity falls to ~34.5%, no mass-harm claims are made, and nothing here is collapse-level.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised and traceable. Adoption is 11→18.1, prices are stalled at $299–349, employer coverage falls 60→43, retatrutide is approved at 28.7%, the 503B exclusion and state limits are in place, 'Quiet' is the marketed feature, and no new indication or safety signal appears. mechanism: Most changes have chains: employer retreat leads to cash orals, which lead to thinness reaching the middle; compounding closure leads to mail importation; the cycling arithmetic reconciles. The aesthetic inversion rests on niche LA/Brooklyn/Austin anecdotes extrapolated to a social 'status' shift. The garbled retatrutide review line ('>12 months after filing as required') is also a flaw. magnitude: Ever-use of 27%, 65+ use of 17% and pediatric use of 0.8% (the claims above) are aggressive for two years, as is a 17-point employer drop in one cycle; the pipeline timing (CagriSema Dec 2026, retatrutide Apr 2028) and prices are in range.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol vignette shows rather than explains: coffee after the pill, the card that pays the electric bill, the coding-dependent coverage, the Long Table, the Windsor pen text, and the Quiet ad on the TV. Implied characters include Hector, the sister, the chef and the photographing diner. Scenes are implied by the casting breakdown, the comedy rooms, couples therapists negotiating dose timing and DoD recruiters.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage for weight management fell to 43% (BGH, 2028 plan year); nearly all employers that dropped it retain coverage under diabetes and CVD codes, so coding at diagnosis now decides who pays.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: a 17-point drop in one year is faster than the 12-point drop of 2025-26, and it is paired with the claim that nearly all droppers keep T2D/CVD coverage, which is asserted rather than shown. The 2027-08 event is also dated before the BGH 2028 survey would normally be fielded.

Magnitude: this is consistent with the +7.1pp driver, but the candidate then stacks a 27% ever-used figure and 37% cycling on it. Those sit uneasily with employer retreat, stalled prices and a cash tier at $299-349 that supposedly lifted the middle income third to 20%.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly 350,000 people are subscribed to programs that sell it as the point.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism/magnitude: Stillwell alone passes 200k subscribers in a year and the total is 350k. The drivers stipulate no new FDA approval, the FDA bars drug-name claims, and Stillwell's own subscriber surveys are the only evidence, so this uptake in about 18 months is asserted, not derived.

rationale.badness: Inequality is the main harm: the two-tier coding system, obesity concentrating in the bottom third, hourly workers losing coverage, and a gray market of unverifiable imported pens (world/access/note, thinness_and_class). Epistemic harm comes from 'quiet' marketing resting on unpublished surveys while no trial measures blunting, and from cycling with no data. Offsets are large: obesity falls, Medicare coverage doubles in the 65+ group, and the inversion is a niche. It reads as a harder society with new losers, not a refusal-level one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible. Adoption is 18.1% (+7.1), prices are stalled, employer coverage retreats, retatrutide is approved at ~28.7%, the inversion is shown in LA/Brooklyn/Austin, restriction appears as age limits, telehealth BMI floors and the 503B exclusion, and Quiet is a marketed feature. The one soft spot is that retatrutide is described as the ~30% pen, though its approval is only Apr 2028. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the arithmetic reconciling ever/current/cycled, income, and cash orals for the middle. Weaker links: the 'aesthetic inversion' rests on narrow trade niches, Quiet's subscriber uptake is asserted, and the price paradox (stalled prices yet middle-income uptake) is only partly explained. magnitude: The 17-point employer drop, 27% ever-used, 17% in the 65+ group and 37% cycled are all at the aggressive edge, and the retatrutide 14-month review plus a Dec 2026 CagriSema approval are plausible but tight. These correspond to claims 1-3, and several of these figures compound one another.

least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ever-use rises from 15% to 27% in two years, and the candidate has 8.9% off now and 37% cycled. This is a very aggressive build on the 7.1pp adoption delta. Adding 7.1pp of current use would more plausibly raise ever-use by roughly 10–12pp, not 12.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage for weight management fell to 43% (BGH, 2028 plan year)
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: a drop from 60% to 43% in two years is steep, though the driver stipulates employer retreat. The related claim that nearly all dropping employers keep diabetes and CVD coverage is convenient, and the candidate also reports a sharp 'cash price stalled' but the '$245 never reached the cash channel' contradicts the parent's stated trend to $245.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly 350,000 people are subscribed to programs that sell it as the point.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: 200,000 subscribers within a year of a March 2027 launch, 350,000 by 2028, sold off-label to non-obese adults at $199 under FDA ad enforcement. The growth is asserted, and the 'passes 200,000 subscribers' event and the 70% 'less noise' claim rest on unpublished surveys.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder two-tier society: coding at diagnosis decides who pays, obesity concentrates in the bottom third, there is a gray-market importation of unverifiable pens, and 350k people are sold chosen flatness with no trial measuring it. Offsetting this, adult obesity falls and the large majority is better off, so it stays near the middle of the scale. Inequality and epistemic scores carry most of the weight (the blunting effect is unmeasured and FDA governs only the ads).
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: adoption of 18.1% matches 11 + 7.1, price stalled with $299–349 cash, employer retreat to 43%, triple agonist at 28.7%, aesthetic inversion, restriction, and marketed-feature personality. Gaps are thin: 'safety_signal: none' is honoured, but the Medicare Bridge extension and the 65+ doubling are not driven by any listed driver. mechanism: most changes have chains (503B closure to importation, coding to coverage), and the ever-used arithmetic is shown and reconciles. Weaker are the culture inversion, sorted to niche LA/Brooklyn/Austin circles yet asserted to reshape casting, and the Quiet subscriber growth. magnitude: ever-use at 27% and cycled-off numbers are aggressive, the 65+ jump from 9% to 17% is large for a $50-copay pilot with ~10% newly eligible, and the 43% employer figure falls fast. Retatrutide filing and approval timing is plausible given the 2027 BLA plan.
rationale.generativity: Marisol, Hector, the Long Table at East Cesar Chavez, the Windsor pen link and the Quiet ad give concrete scenes with strong texture and implied conflict about cost and coding. The world fields add casting, comedy, couples-therapy and dosing-negotiation vignettes that could each become a film. The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains, though the ending is slightly neat.
